targeting.title: Could Not Connect to Ollama App, Is It Running? Fixes by OS
targeting.metaTitle: Could Not Connect to Ollama? Fixes by OS
targeting.metaDescription: Fix "could not connect to ollama app, is it running?" and the newer ollama serve error. What each message means on Windows, Linux, macOS, Docker and WSL.
targeting.excerpt: What "could not connect to ollama app, is it running?" and its newer variants mean, checked against the Ollama 0.40.16 source: a message lookup table, the fix for Windows, Linux, macOS, Docker and WSL, the OLLAMA_HOST defaults, and why ollama serve reports the address in use.
targeting.keywords: could not connect to ollama app is it running, could not connect to ollama server, ollama could not connect to a running ollama instance, ollama serve address already in use, ollama timed out waiting for server to start, ollama connection refused 11434, ollama upgrade in progress, could not locate ollama app, ollama_host 0.0.0.0, ollama port 11434, ollama server not responding, how to start ollama server
targeting.summary: The message means the ollama command got no reply on port 11434 and could not start the server; start the app on Windows or macOS, or the systemd service on Linux|The wording depends on version and system: one fixed sentence up to 0.7.0, a prefixed cause from 0.7.1, and the cause alone from 0.15.5|OLLAMA_HOST is read by the command as well as the server, and ollama serve reporting the address in use means a server is already running
targeting.author: Ali Rehman

competitors.gap: No competitor links to the Ollama source. None gives the exact releases where the wording changed (0.7.1 and 0.15.5) together with per-system fixes. None covers the Windows 'upgrade in progress...' message or the lookup order for ollama app.exe. Only one mentions the 'could not connect to a running Ollama instance' warning. This article is organised as a message lookup, which none of them is.

primarySourceNotes: cmd/cmd.go at v0.40.16: checkServerHeartbeat is the PreRunE of 13 commands (show, run, stop, pull, push, signin, login, signout, logout, list, ps, cp, rm). A heartbeat error containing ' refused' or 'could not connect' triggers startApp; any other error is returned unchanged. versionHandler prints 'Warning: could not connect to a running Ollama instance'. RunServer calls net.Listen on envconfig.Host().
api/client.go: ClientFromEnvironment uses envconfig.Host(), not ConnectableHost(); Heartbeat is an HTTP HEAD to '/'. server/routes.go answers HEAD and GET '/' with 'Ollama is running'.
cmd/start.go: waitForServer ticks every 500 ms and times out after 5 s with 'timed out waiting for server to start'.

cmd/start_windows.go: 'upgrade in progress...' when OllamaSetup.exe runs; looks for 'ollama app.exe' beside the executable, then %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama, then PATH ('could not locate ollama app'); 'unable to start ollama app'.

cmd/start_darwin.go (v0.15.5 and v0.40.16, identical files): returns the ollama serve message unless the executable is a symlink into Ollama.app; v0.15.4 returned 'could not find ollama app'. cmd/start_default.go always returns the ollama serve message.

Version history, checked release by release: v0.7.0 cmd.go replaces every startApp error with 'could not connect to ollama app, is it running?'; v0.7.1 through v0.15.4 wrap it as 'ollama server not responding - %w'; v0.15.5 and later return the cause alone. An earlier draft said 0.16.0; probing v0.15.1 to v0.15.6 corrected it.

envconfig/config.go: default http://127.0.0.1:11434; no scheme means http and port 11434; http:// defaults to port 80 and https:// to 443; ConnectableHost exists with a comment that connecting to unspecified addresses fails on Windows.

Local Windows 11 (build 26300) checks: Win32 error 10061 text 'No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it'; error 10048 text 'Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted'; a Node 24 TCP connection to 0.0.0.0 reached listeners bound to 127.0.0.1 and to 0.0.0.0.
Microsoft Learn WSL networking page: NAT mode needs the host IP to reach Windows apps from Linux; mirrored mode allows localhost in both directions.
